response.sql: WITH rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS overall_mean FROM rating_avg) SELECT r.rating, r.avg_rate_per_day, r.avg_rate_per_day - o.overall_mean AS above_overall_mean FROM rating_avg r CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE r.avg_rate_per_day > o.overall_mean ORDER BY r.rating;

assumptions.assumption: The threshold 'at least 20.99' is inclusive (replacement_cost >= 20.99) and applies to film.replacement_cost, so the averages are taken over films, not over inventory copies.

Missing values are handled by AVG, which skips NULL per-film quotients. rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL in the schema, and rental_duration is 3 to 7 in the data, so no division by zero occurs. Ratings with no qualifying films produce no group and are excluded from the overall mean.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages, as the request states, so a rating with more films does not count more.
